thread:
jess: Hey y'all, seeing intermittent 400s from /v1/embeddings in prod over the last 3 hours. Errors look like "embedding dimension mismatch: expected 1536 got 768". Seems correlated with traffic spikes and large batched requests. Anyone else seeing this?

alex: Noted. Can you paste a raw request id + sample payload and the exact error log?

jess: Sure — one example: request_id=req_20260301_4232
jess: Payload had 3 items: one long document (~45k chars) + two short strings. Using model `open-embed-large-1536` (we think). Here's the runtime log around the failure:

```
2026-03-01T14:02:11Z [batcher] coalesced batch=3 requests=[rA,rB,rC]
2026-03-01T14:02:11Z [batcher] models_in_batch=[open-embed-large-1536, open-embed-small-768, open-embed-large-1536]
2026-03-01T14:02:11Z [runtime] ERROR embedding_dim_mismatch: expected=1536 observed=768 request=rB
2026-03-01T14:02:11Z [runtime] responding 400 -> client
```

alex: Interesting — batcher should normally group by model family. Looks like we coalesced mismatched model variants into one batch. Was the client explicitly setting model per-item or per-request?

jess: Our customers send multiple inputs in one call (list of texts) to the embeddings endpoint (typical). We expected server to keep them in the same model; we didn't set per-item model field.

michael: tagging eng-runtime. From logs it looks like coalescer grouped requests across model variants because the upstream shim omitted output_dim metadata when model alias used. That means coalescer only saw model alias and not resolved output size, so mixed dims slipped in.

eng-runtime: Confirmed. Reproducer: ran a local load test with three requests where one used alias `open-embed-small` (maps to 768), two used `open-embed-large` (1536). When the alias was present but the full model meta not attached, the coalescer grouped them incorrectly.

eng-runtime: Short-term mitigations we can do immediately:
- add a validation in the coalescer to reject batches that contain different `output_dim` values (fast fail, return 400)
- for Hosted customers, flip `coalesce_by_full_model_meta=true` (will increase batch fragmentation but prevents mismatch)
- doc change to encourage clients to keep homogeneous model usage per request

alex: Can you share the curl we used to repro? I'll paste it in case customers need a clear repro to try locally.

eng-runtime: Repro curl (staging):
```
curl -X POST https://staging.api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxxxx' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"open-embed-large","input":["<long doc>","short1","short2"]}'
```

eng-runtime: The payload above triggers dynamic batching where the coalescer fetches model metadata lazily; if metadata resolution race occurs, we sometimes end up combining requests with different resolved dims.

tara: I repro'd on staging. Also noticed tail latency spikes around the same times — when big docs come through the coalescer pads smaller inputs to match max sequence length and PINs the batch so it waits longer. That plus occasional batch failures causes retry storms.

alex: Immediate customer-facing workarounds suggested:
- Set client `max_batch_size: 1` for embeddings (call-level option) if you need strict isolation
- Ensure each request uses the exact model id (not alias) so server resolves dims deterministically
- If using SDK, set `embeddings: { prefer_homogeneous_batch: true }` (we'll add to docs)

jess: For the specific customer, I patched their proxy to send single-item requests and errors stopped. But that's a painful cost hit. Would prefer server-side fix.

eng-runtime: Plan: implement fast validation to reject mixed-dimension batches (rollout in next 6 hours) + a canary of metadata eager-resolution path (PR #4567). Longer-term: change coalescer to group by (model_id, output_dim) and add telemetry to surface mixed-dimation coalescing attempts.

michael: Can support prepare rollback steps in case canary affects latency? Also request that eng-runtime add a feature flag so we can toggle `coalesce_by_output_dim` per-customer.

eng-runtime: Yup flag will be in the canary. We'll also add a temporary server-side override for Dedicated/Private customers in console.

support-bot: Escalation created: INC-2026-031-78. Labels: embeddings, dynbatch, severity=medium. Assigned: eng-runtime, support.

alex: I'll email the affected customer with a mitigation note (suggesting single-item calls or forcing explicit model id) and timeline: hotfix + canary tonight, full rollout tomorrow morning UTC.

tara: Repro notes saved to staging-run-8923. Key logs and `strace` dump attached there.

jess: Thanks everyone — please ping here when the canary is live so I can update the customer.

eng-runtime: Will do. Planning canary at 22:00 UTC, monitoring CPU and batch fragmentation metrics. If you see regressions, ping ENG-RUNTIME directly.

jess: ack :thumbsup:
